name: Polyostotic Fibrous Dysplasia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Fibrous Dysplasia

criteria.description: Presence of fibrous dysplasia lesions involving two or more bones
Radiographic evidence of ground-glass appearance and bone expansion
Histological confirmation showing fibrous tissue replacing normal bone
Association with McCune-Albright syndrome features (café-au-lait spots, endocrinopathies)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of polyostotic bone lesions with characteristic radiographic features; histopathology supportive but not mandatory
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for GNAS mutations can support diagnosis but is not routinely required

laboratory: Elevated serum alkaline phosphatase in active disease
imaging: Radiographs showing ground-glass bone lesions with cortical thinning
CT scan demonstrating expansile fibrous lesions
MRI for assessment of soft tissue and nerve involvement
other: Histopathology showing irregular woven bone trabeculae in fibrous stroma without osteoblastic rimming

distinguishingFeatures: Involvement of a single bone rather than multiple bones
Less severe deformities and fewer systemic manifestations
Typically affects tibia and fibula in children
Histology shows osteoblastic rimming unlike fibrous dysplasia
Radiographic features include mixed lytic and sclerotic lesions with cortical thickening
Elevated serum alkaline phosphatase with different clinical presentation

redFlags: New onset neurological deficits indicating nerve compression
Signs of malignant transformation such as sudden increase in pain or swelling
